title: Bulk and microphase separation in chiral active systems
authors: Sumeja Bureković, S. J. Kole, Ananyo Maitra, Cesare Nardini
abstract: Many active particles phase-separate due to quorum-sensing interactions, and their self-propulsion mechanisms often break chiral symmetry. Using particle and continuum models, we uncover the role of chirality in inducing bulk or microphase separation, including a chiral phase formed of vapor bubbles. Analytical predictions for the emergence of these phases require a coarse-graining technique based on multiple-scale analysis. Further, introducing a minimal active field theory, we show that, in the bulk phase separation regime, chirality does not alter the diffusive $t^{1/3}$ coarsening law nor the dynamical exponent associated with capillary waves, but induces traveling waves at the interface. We finally demonstrate that, even in the absence of fluid flows, chirality can cause the breakup of elongated droplets, resembling phenomena previously observed experimentally.
summary: This work analyzes how chirality affects phase separation in self-propelled active matter. Using sophisticated continuum models and multi-scale analysis, the authors distinguish between bulk and microphase separation regimes. The key finding is that chirality introduces novel dynamic features, such as interface traveling waves and droplet splitting, even when fluid flows are absent.
main_problem: The study investigates how chirality influences phase separation—specifically distinguishing between bulk and microphase regimes—in active particle systems driven by quorum-sensing interactions.
main_result: Chirality is shown to induce traveling waves at the interface and can cause elongated droplets to split even without fluid flows, a phenomenon distinct from achiral systems.
method: The analysis employs both Diffusion-Drift (DD) approximation and advanced Multiple-Scales (MS) coarse-graining techniques applied to continuum models of active particles.
model_or_system: The system involves Chiral Quorum-Sensing Active Particles (cQSAPs) modeled by particle dynamics and a continuum description called chiral Active Model B (cAMB).
key_observables: Phase separation types (bulk vs. microphase), coarsening law ($\ell_{typ} \propto t^{1/3}$), interfacial tensions, and the growth rate $r(q)$ from linear stability analysis.
important_parameters: Chirality parameter ($\omega$), translational diffusivity ($DT$), and density ($ho_0$).
main_assumptions: The DD approximation is insufficient, necessitating the use of MS theory for accurate prediction of microphase separation; the MS expansion itself has limitations near instability thresholds.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the phase diagram showing stability predictions (DD vs. MS), time evolution of coarsening ($\ell_{typ} \propto t^{1/3}$), and simulation snapshots demonstrating droplet splitting.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical model (cQSAPs) to comparing theoretical approaches (DD vs. MS theory) for stability analysis, culminating in showing how chirality modifies dynamics like interface wave propagation and droplet breakup.
why_interesting: While focused on classical active matter, the use of advanced non-equilibrium statistical mechanics tools like multiple-scale expansion and linear stability analysis mirrors techniques used to study pattern formation and phase transitions in quantum many-body systems.
